title: Qualitative Paper ELONA Test
author: Manuela De Las Casas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8f7htrn
materials: This will be the test method number 1.

steps.title: Prepare Wax Dots on Nitrocellulose
steps.instruction: Create wax-delimited areas on a nitrocellulose strip using a hot plate.

substeps.instruction: Set hot plate to 100ºC (or temperature sufficient to melt wax).
Place a small amount of wax pencil on a Petri dish on the hot plate until melted.
Cut a nitrocellulose sheet to the desired size.
Dip the pointy side of a 200μL pipette tip into the melted wax and press the broad end onto the nitrocellulose strip to create a wax circle.
Repeat to create all necessary dots for the assay.
Sandwich the strip between two sheets of paper and place on the hot plate with a Petri dish on top for pressure.
Warm for 5 minutes to allow wax penetration, then cool.
Verify that the center of the circles is clear.

steps.title: Prepare Aptamer Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the biotinylated Apta-Eco and digoxigenin-tagged RC-dig aptamer mixture.

substeps.instruction: In an Eppendorf tube, mix Apta-Eco (biotin tag) and RC-dig (digoxigenin tag) at equal concentrations (e.g., 100 μM stock).
Add Aptamer Buffer (PBS, 1.4 mM Mg 2+) in a 1:1:3 proportion (Apta-Eco:RC-dig:Buffer).
Heat the mix in a tube on a hot plate at 95ºC for 5 minutes.
Cool the tube on ice.
Mix the cooled solution 1:1 with streptavidin 0.2 μg/μL (18μM).
Incubate on ice for a few minutes to allow protein and aptamer bonding.

steps.title: Apply Reagents to Membrane Dots
steps.instruction: Apply specific reagents to the prepared wax dots according to the experimental method or control group.

substeps.instruction: Method 2: Pipette 5 μL of the aptamer-streptavidin mix into dots (2-3 dots per concentration) and dry completely.
Method 3: Pipette 5 μL of Apta-Eco, dry; then pipette 5 μL of RC-dig aptamer and dry.
Additional Section: Add 5 μL of the mix to reserved dots, dry; then add 5 μL of 10 μM RC-dig and dry.
Negative Control 1: Pipette 5 μL of 0.1 μg/mL streptavidin and dry.
Negative Control 2: Pipette 5 μL of 0.1 μg/mL streptavidin and dry.
Positive Control 3: Pipette 5 μL of 0.1 μg/mL streptavidin and dry; then add 5 μL of antibody (Anti-Dig-POD 1:100 in PBS 1.4mM Mg 2+ BSA 0.2%).
Negative Control 4: Pipette 5 μL of 0.1 μg/mL streptavidin, dry; then 5 μL of Apta-Eco, dry; then 5 μL of RC-dig aptamer, dry.
Other reserved dots: Pipette 5 μL of 0.1 μg/mL (10μM) streptavidin and dry completely.

steps.title: Block Membrane
steps.instruction: Block free spaces on the membrane to prevent non-specific binding.

substeps.instruction: Place the strip in a Petri dish and pipette 5% BSA (in PBS) over it.
Use tweezers to move the strip gently to ensure blocking of free spaces and pipette away excess liquid.
Allow to dry slightly (not soaked, but not perfectly dry).
Perform this for all methods and Negative Controls 1 and 2; do NOT block Positive Control 3.

steps.title: Incubate with Antibody
steps.instruction: Apply the detection antibody and incubate in a humid environment.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5 μL of antibody (Anti-Dig-POD 1:100 in PBS 1.4 mM Mg 2+ BSA 0.2%) onto the dots (skip for Negative Controls 1 and 4).
Incubate for one hour in a humid chamber (e.g., Petri dish with wet paper) to prevent complete drying.

steps.title: Wash and Develop Signal
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane and apply ABTS for color development.

substeps.instruction: Remove strips from the chamber and wash with PBS by pipetting excess liquid and moving gently with tweezers (skip for Negative Controls 1 and 4).
Allow to dry partially.
Place strips back in the humid chamber and pipette 10 μL of ABTS on each dot.
Incubate for 30 minutes (can be shortened to 15 min if reaction is fast, or extended by 15 min if no color develops).

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Analyze
steps.instruction: Terminate the reaction and quantify the results.

substeps.instruction: Dry all strips on a hot plate at 95ºC for 5 minutes to stop the reaction simultaneously.
Scan the strips for higher quality results.
Analyze dot density using software tools.
